subject: history_social
passage: In ancient Mesopotamia, scribes wrote by pressing marks into tablets of soft clay. Many tablets were simply left to dry in the sun, and sun-dried clay can crumble or turn back into mud if it gets wet. Strong heat, however, hardens clay into a material much like pottery. When the city of Nineveh was burned by invading armies in 612 BCE, the fire may have ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: led scribes to stop writing on clay and start writing on stone.
choices.B: softened the tablets so that their marks could no longer be read.
choices.C: destroyed every clay tablet that had been stored in the city.
choices.D: helped preserve some tablets by baking them hard.

explanation.why: Sun-dried tablets are fragile, but strong heat turns clay hard like pottery. A large fire would have supplied that heat, so it could have made some tablets more durable.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says nothing about scribes switching to stone.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This reverses the text, which says heat hardens clay rather than softening it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says heat hardens clay, so a fire would not necessarily destroy the tablets.
explanation.D: Correct. Strong heat hardens clay, so the fire could have baked some tablets into a lasting form.
